articles.title_original: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
articles.title_zh: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
facts_zh:
Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
- Published
US Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections.
Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership".
Schumer, 75, has led Democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader.

all_titles.en: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge

articles.title_original: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
articles.title_zh: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
facts_zh:
German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
- Published
Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation.
Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers.
But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara Bünger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police.

all_titles.en: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad

articles.title_zh: At least 24 killed after bus collides with truck in north-east India
facts_zh:
At least 24 killed after bus collides with truck in north-east India
- Published
At least 24 people have died and 11 others injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India.
The accident happened near Kaziranga National Park, a Unesco World Heritage site, and the injured have been admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.
Several of the deceased are college students, according to Assam's rural development minister Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

articles.title_zh: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over uninspected Iran nuclear site
facts_zh:
UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over uninspected Iran nuclear site
- Published
The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect.
Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of Isfahan a day before Israel began attacking its nuclear sites last June.
The US joined the strikes later that month.

facts_zh:
Rosalía scoops historic third best album award at Latin Grammys
- Published
Spanish star Rosalía has made history as the first woman to win the best album award at the Latin Grammys three times, after being recognised for her project Lux.
The singer took home five trophies in total, including two for her track La Perla which was named song of the year and best pop song.
La Perla was also nominated for record of the year but missed out to Argentine singer Milo J's song Niño.

articles.title_original: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
articles.title_zh: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
facts_zh: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain.
Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November.
A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours.

articles.title_original: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
articles.title_zh: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
facts_zh:
African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
- Published
Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall and several other contestants from Africa could miss this year's competition in Puerto Rico as they race to secure a US visa.
Hall is due to represent Zimbabwe at the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, with the winner set to be crowned on 24 November.
But she has yet to obtain a visa to travel to the US territory.

all_titles.en: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
